item.research_question: How does increasing the configurational disorder (number of first-row transition metals) in spinel oxides affect CO oxidation activity and long-term stability compared to lower entropy variants?
item.material_system: Spinel oxides (M3O4) with M = Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn; specifically 4-metal (CrMnFeCo)3O4, 5-metal (CrMnFeCoNi)3O4, 6-metal (CrMnFeCoNiCu)3O4, and 7-metal (CrMnFeCoNiCuZn)3O4
item.processing_route: Solventless thermolysis of equimolar metal diethyldithiocarbamate precursors dissolved in dichloromethane, heated to 900 °C (15 °C min−1 ramp rate) in static air, and held for 4 h
item.test_conditions: Plug-flow reactor, total flow 50 mL min−1, feed gas 1 vol.% CO, 5 vol.% O2, Ar balance; temperature ramp 50 to 650 °C at 10 °C min−1; stability test held for 14 h at temperatures below T50 (e.g., 208 °C for 7-metal)
key_findings: The 7-metal HESO showed a T10 value of 168 °C, which was a 63% decrease compared to the 4-metal MESO (454 °C).
The 7-metal HESO exhibited a T50 value of 250 °C, which was 56% lower than the 5-metal HESO (569 °C).
During 14 h of operation, the 7-metal spinel oxide showed a decrease in activity of only 4.7% ± 0.3%, whereas the 4-metal variant decreased by 12.2% ± 0.4%.
The 7-metal HESO saw an improvement in CO conversion with a rate of +0.62 ± 0.13% h−1 between 0 and 2 h, while the 4-metal spinel oxide decreased at −0.85 ± 0.07% h−1.
Rietveld refinement determined the lattice parameter for the 7-metal HESO as 8.33 Å, decreasing as the number of metals increased.
A minor monoclinic CuO secondary phase (5.0 ± 0.3 wt.%) was observed in the 6- and 7-metal samples.

Post-catalysis XPS showed the ratio of the second oxygen environment (OB, M-OR/OV) to lattice oxygen (OA) decreased for all samples, but the 6- and 7-metal HESOs maintained higher ratios than lower entropy systems.
item.mechanism: The authors propose that adding cations that prefer tetrahedral sites (Ni, Cu, Zn) drives multi-valent, catalytically active metals (Mn, Fe) out of tetrahedral sites and into octahedral sites, which are more prevalent at the surface. Additionally, higher disorder correlates with an increase in oxygen vacancies, which helps regulate the generation of reactive oxygen species in catalytic oxidation reactions proceeding via the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism.
item.limitations: The study was conducted under dry conditions; industrially realistic feeds containing catalyst poisons such as sulfur and water are known to cause significant deactivation and were not tested. Some Cr segregation was observed at the nanoscale, and a small amount of CuO secondary phase formed in the 6- and 7-metal samples.
item.future_work: Ongoing operando investigations of more complex reactions (such as Fischer-Tropsch), synchrotron-based cation distribution analysis, and testing with realistic reaction feeds containing catalyst poisons such as water.
quotes: A substantial 63% decrease in the T10 value (temperature to reach 10% CO oxidation) is observed by systematically increasing the number of first‐row transition metals within the spinel oxide.
The 7‐metal HESO showed a T10 value of 168 °C, which was 63% lower than the 4‐metal MESO (at 454 °C), and a T50 value of 250 °C, which was 56% lower than the 5‐metal HESO (at 569 °C).

The addition of cations that prefer tetrahedral sites might drive multi‐valent, catalytically active metals (e.g., Mn and Fe) out of tetrahedral sites and into octahedral sites, which are more prevalent at the surface, thereby potentially enhancing catalytic activity.

Mechanism: The authors propose that adding cations that prefer tetrahedral sites (Ni, Cu, Zn) drives multi-valent, catalytically active metals (Mn, Fe) out of tetrahedral sites and into octahedral sites, which are more prevalent at the surface. Additionally, higher disorder correlates with an increase in oxygen vacancies, which helps regulate the generation of reactive oxygen species in catalytic oxidation reactions proceeding via the Mars–van Krevelen mechanism.. Limitations: The study was conducted under dry conditions; industrially realistic feeds containing catalyst poisons such as sulfur and water are known to cause significant deactivation and were not tested. Some Cr segregation was observed at the nanoscale, and a small amount of CuO secondary phase formed in the 6- and 7-metal samples..
